answer: Attention Drift Clock. Each identity must answer randomized micro-challenges drawn from a private yarrow-indexed pool at unpredictable intervals; response latency and miss rate accumulate into a drift score. An inlet admits only agents whose drift stays under threshold across a rolling window, so operators must staff continuous monitoring per identity. The per-identity cost is sustained human-or-model attention around the clock; a zephyr of occasional check-ins fails, and scaling to N identities multiplies that attention linearly, making sybil farms economically unviable.
